00 / PROJECT

The control code is already built.
This site shows how it behaves.

The underlying course implementation lives in the team’s original course repository. This showcase brings its architecture, recorded run, and interactive railway behavior together in one place.

01 / SYSTEM

From a sensor edge
to a safe next action.

The showcase follows the project’s operating loop: observe the railway, attribute an event, update train state, evaluate conflict, then issue or await an action.

STATE / 01

Two-train coordination

Independent speed and direction states are reconciled against shared track.

Concurrent control

INPUT / 02

Sensor attribution

Reservation owner and generation identify a train; unreserved rising events stay unattributed rather than being guessed.

Fail-closed observation

TRACK / 03

Turnout control

Switch state is visible before a train reaches a branching decision.

Straight / curved

SAFETY / 04

Conflict response

Head-on risk stops both trains; a following conflict holds the rear train until movement authority returns.

Following / head-on / authority

RECOVERY / 05

Reroute & remove

The project console can safely stop and replan from CURRENT, cancel, remove, or block track from dispatch.

Operator in the loop

PRESENTATION / 06

System clarity

The film captures the physical run while the interactive desk makes each state change easy to explore.

See every decision

PHYSICAL RAILWAY / RECORDED DEMOVIDEO

TWO-TRAIN DEMO

The recording documents two trains leaving their starting positions without assigned destinations. Speeds and upcoming turnout choices vary as the run develops.

  1. 00

    Dispatch

    Two trains begin with independent, variable speeds.

  2. 01

    Turnout ahead

    A switch changes before the approaching train reaches it.

  3. 02

    Same-direction conflict

    A following train waits when the shared segment is not clear.

  4. 03

    Opposing risk

    Both trains stop and wait for operator intervention.

  5. 04

    Recover

    The terminal can reroute or remove a train to release the hold.

04 / TRACK REFERENCE

The physical layout,
translated into data.

Official course diagrams ground the project in a finite graph of sensors, branches, and turnout states.

GRAPH VIEW

Nodes become observations.
Edges become decisions.

The course files describe directed nodes and edges with distances in millimetres. This original redraw and the simulator reduce that topology to a legible explanatory view.

CONCERNPROJECT BEHAVIOR PRESENTEDWEB REPRESENTATION
ObservationReservation owner + generation attribute sensor events; unknown events stay unknown.Named sensor markers and an explicit attribution log.
Shared trackAtomic rolling-authority windows reserve both node directions.A highlighted conflict zone and visible hold state.
Traffic policyFollowing holds the rear train; head-on risk stops both.Three selectable scenarios with recoverable states.
Recoveryreroute registers a CURRENT-based replacement after a safe stop; go submits it. Without a trusted pose, the project stays fail-stopped. Operator-declared remove releases the active plan and authority.A safe subset of the console vocabulary.
REPOSITORY EVIDENCE / 01

State-rich dispatch

The dispatcher models staged, waiting, preparing, running, braking, arrived, failed, and traffic-hold states rather than a single “moving” flag.

REPOSITORY EVIDENCE / 02

Atomic authority

Rolling reservation windows are updated by generation and include the reverse node to prevent opposite-direction physical overlap.

REPOSITORY EVIDENCE / 03

Console vocabulary

dispatch, go, trips, reroute, cancel, remove, block, and trackview are present in the completed project branch.

VALIDATION / 04

Route testing workflow

Software route simulations, sensor state, and calibration checks support iterative testing across Track B.
